rationale: Timer bookkeeping: the rebuild sets the time since the compressor stopped back to 0 when the compressor STARTS. Setting line says that time starts again from 0 when the compressor turns off, and does not change while it runs. Never visible as heating or cooling in these situations, but a misread of a clear line.
With no strips fitted, the rebuild gives no heat at all even with the outdoor temperature well above the cut-off. "No heat runs" belongs only to the cut-off rule.

Below the outdoor cut-off, with the room only 2 degrees below the setting: the correct program runs the strips as the only heat whenever heat is called for (his rule 7); the rebuild still waits for 3 degrees below (his rule 6). Both rules are his and the wording allows both readings. Not a fair question; a word for him to settle.
